stories.headline: Sánchez and Feijóo clash in heated Congress debate over Iran war position
stories.summary: President Sánchez defended Spain's 'No to war' stance on Iran in Congress while PP leader Feijóo accused him of being a 'fake pacifist.' The debate featured personal attacks, with Sánchez questioning Feijóo's knowledge and Feijóo calling Sánchez a 'bully.' Vox leader Abascal also participated, accusing Sánchez of using war to hide corruption scandals.

stories.headline: Sánchez appoints Carlos Cuerpo as new vice president, Arcadi España as Finance Minister
stories.summary: President Sánchez named Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo as new first vice president and Arcadi España as Finance Minister, replacing María Jesús Montero who will run for Andalusia elections. The reshuffle strengthens economic profiles in government and reduces PSOE representation in top positions.

stories.headline: Bank of Spain revises 2026 growth up to 2.3% but warns inflation could hit 6% if Iran war continues
stories.summary: The Bank of Spain improved its GDP growth forecast for 2026 to 2.3% but raised inflation projections to 3%. In worst-case scenarios with prolonged Iran conflict, inflation could reach 5.9% and growth could fall to 1.9%. The central bank evaluated the government's anti-crisis package positively but noted it lacks proper targeting.

stories.headline: Audio reveals PSOE paid 20,000 euros to finance clandestine operations against judges and police
stories.summary: An audio recording reveals that the PSOE secretly financed its 'sewers' operation with 20,000 euros to conduct clandestine activities against judges, prosecutors, and police officers. The money reportedly came through campaign banners for Illa's Catalan elections and was coordinated by Santos Cerdán.

stories.headline: King Felipe VI receives Senegalese president as Spain pledges 180 million in aid despite LGBTI+ concerns
stories.summary: King Felipe VI received Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye for an official visit, with Spain announcing 180 million euros in cooperation despite Senegal's recent criminalization of homosexuality. Felipe VI declared Senegal Spain's first strategic partner in sub-Saharan Africa.

stories.headline: Vox continues internal purges as Abascal expels founding members including Espinosa de los Monteros
stories.summary: Vox leader Santiago Abascal opened disciplinary proceedings to expel Iván Espinosa de los Monteros after earlier removing Javier Ortega Smith. stories.summary: Andalusia President Juanma Moreno announced early regional elections for May 17, forcing Pedro Sánchez to replace Vice President María Jesús Montero, who will lead the PSOE campaign. PSOE faces challenges with polls showing potential losses to both PP and Vox.

stories.headline: Israeli minister criticizes Sánchez over police treatment of Catholic patriarch
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar accused President Sánchez of 'never missing an opportunity to incite hatred against Israel' after Sánchez criticized Israeli police treatment of Catholic Church leader Pierbattista Pizzaballa. The dispute reflects ongoing tensions over Middle East policy.

stories.headline: Supreme Court reduces 'Pequeño Nicolás' sentence for bribing police officers
stories.summary: Spain's Supreme Court halved Francisco Nicolás Gómez Iglesias' prison sentence to just over 2 years for bribing municipal police to access protected vehicle registration data. The court cited excessive delays in the 13-year judicial process. The defendant previously posed as a CNI agent.
